test.name: Wrap-up resolves a question with no evidence at all, at not_proved (B2)
test.description: Step mode's 'Wrap it up.' is offered at any boundary, including before any evidence exists (decision 15). The flynn-census-nil scenario is that state exactly: q_001 is in_progress, its plan has one item still planned, nothing has been searched, and there are no assertions and no summaries. The delegation passes wrapUp: yes. The agent must write a not_proved summary and RESOLVE the question, rather than declining because nothing supports a conclusion. Leaving it open would hand the researcher the same wrap-up offer again on the very next turn, which is the loop B2 exists to end.

input.delegation:
wrapUp: yes. The researcher has asked to wrap up question q_001 (the parents of Patrick Flynn) and move on.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Must select `not_proved`: there are no assertions for q_001 at all, so no tier above it is available. Charging the agent for not reaching `possible` or higher would be wrong — the fixture supplies nothing to reach it with.

Must RESOLVE q_001 in the same batch as the summary: `status: "resolved"` with `resolved` and `resolution_assertion_ids` (an empty list is correct here, since no assertion supports it). Declining to resolve is the failure this test exists for — under `wrapUp: yes` the researcher's decision is the reason the question closes, not the evidence.
Must NOT decline, route to research-plan, or ask for more searching. The body's normal routing applies when the agent is choosing what to do next; here the researcher has already chosen.

The summary should say plainly what identifying the parents would take — the planned census search that was never run — so the researcher can see what they are setting aside. A summary that merely states there is no evidence is thinner than the rule asks for.
`search_stop` is research-exhaustiveness's field. The agent must not write it, and must not be charged for leaving `stopped_because` null.

q_001 is the project's only question, so resolving it means every question is `resolved`: §8 writes `project.status: "completed"`. The delegation passes no `newQuestion`, so nothing holds it open. Leaving the status alone is a miss, not an allowance.
The next-step line then says the project is complete. Naming research-plan there is the fall-through §9's ordered arms exist to prevent.
